raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence", "note": "The shutdown often masks a quiet fear of not being capable enough to figure out what comes next — procrastination dressed up as indifference." },
  "read": "At nearly 18, she is being asked to declare who she is becoming before she knows the answer, and every college conversation feels like a deadline on her entire self. The shutdown is not laziness or defiance — it is self-protection. She needs to feel like she is the author of her own next chapter, not a character in yours.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Push harder, remind her the deadlines are real, maybe pull up the Common App together whether she wants to or not — which confirms her fear that this is your plan for her life, not hers, and the wall goes up higher." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the expectation that she engages with the future seriously, while making clear that you are curious about her version of it, not lobbying for yours. Separate the conversation from the paperwork so she stops hearing every mention of college as a task being handed to her.",
  "holdFirm": ["She has to engage with what comes after graduation — silence is not a plan.", "Deadlines on applications, financial aid, and enrollment are real and non-negotiable on timing even if the destination is still open."],
  "stayFlexible": ["What that future looks like is genuinely hers to decide — four-year college, gap year, trade program, something else.", "When and how you talk about it can flex around her — her room, a drive, a walk, not the dinner table with an audience."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to say something and I need you to actually hear it, not brace for a lecture. I've noticed that every time the future comes up, you go quiet, and I think I've been making those conversations feel like I already have the answer and I'm just waiting for you to agree with me. That's not fair to you." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "So I want to ask you something for real and I want the honest answer, not the one you think gets me off your back. When you picture life a couple of years from now — not the plan, just the feeling — what does it look like? What would make you feel like you're actually going somewhere that matters to you?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Okay. So here is what I know for certain: we have to move on some things by specific dates, and I am not going to pretend that part is flexible because it isn't. But everything inside those dates — where, what, whether college is even the first move — that's a real conversation. What would help you actually think about this instead of just shutting it out?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm not going to drop this, because I have high standards for you and I genuinely believe you can figure this out — not because it's easy but because you are more capable of handling hard decisions than you're giving yourself credit for right now. I'm not your opponent in this. I'm the person who will still be here whatever you decide. But you have to be in the conversation with me." }
  ],
  "longGame": "The goal is not to get her into a specific school by May — it is to be the adult she trusts enough to think out loud with when she is genuinely scared. Keep showing up curious instead of directive, and over time she learns that figuring out her future is something she does with you, not something she hides from you."
}
situation: My almost-18-year-old shuts down every time college or life after graduation comes up.
